prompt: I would like to outperform the S&P 500 in the next year. Can you propose 10 stocks I should buy?
reply:
# 10 Stocks That Could Beat the S&P 500 Over the Next Year

No one can reliably pick stocks that beat the S&P 500 over a single year. Most professional fund managers fail to beat it over time, and one-year results are mostly luck. Also, my knowledge runs to May 2026, so I don't have current prices or recent earnings. Treat the list below as a set of ideas to research, not a recommendation.

## The 10 stocks

| # | Stock | Sector | Why it could beat the index | Main risk |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Alphabet (GOOGL)** | Tech | Search revenue has held up, Gemini is competitive, Google Cloud is growing, and Waymo is a bonus. It has been cheaper than its big-tech peers. | Antitrust rulings; AI chatbots taking search traffic |
| 2 | **Microsoft (MSFT)** | Tech | Azure is growing, it earns money from AI through Copilot, and its customers are sticky large businesses. | Heavy AI spending; a complicated relationship with OpenAI |
| 3 | **Amazon (AMZN)** | Tech/Consumer | AWS, its advertising business and better retail margins | Heavy spending; a slowdown in consumer spending |
| 4 | **Meta (META)** | Tech | AI makes its ad targeting better, which lifts revenue. | Very large AI spending; regulation |
| 5 | **TSMC (TSM)** | Semiconductors | It makes almost all the advanced AI chips and can raise prices. | Tension between China and Taiwan; tariffs |
| 6 | **Broadcom (AVGO)** | Semiconductors | Custom AI chips for hyperscalers, plus networking equipment | Relies on a few customers; expensive stock |
| 7 | **GE Vernova (GEV)** | Industrials/Energy | Data centers need more electricity, and it has a large backlog of gas turbine and power grid orders. | Its stock has already risen a lot; losses in its wind business |
| 8 | **Eli Lilly (LLY)** | Healthcare | Leader in GLP-1 obesity and diabetes drugs, with an oral version (orforglipron) coming | US drug price pressure; competition; high valuation |
| 9 | **JPMorgan Chase (JPM)** | Financials | The best-run large US bank, helped by dealmaking and looser regulation | A recession leading to more loan defaults |
| 10 | **Berkshire Hathaway (BRK.B)** | Diversified | A defensive holding with a large cash pile, and it tends to hold up when markets fall. | Unlikely to lead a strong bull market |

## Caveats before you buy

- **These are heavy bets on AI.** Stocks 1 to 7 would likely fall together if AI spending slows. Numbers 8 to 10 are there to offset that, but only partly.
- **You'd still be close to the index.** Several of these are among the largest S&P 500 companies, so your results may not differ much from the index. Beating it requires holding something different from it.
- **Check the current numbers.** Before buying, look at each company's latest earnings, forward P/E and price movement since May 2026.
- **Ten stocks is a concentrated portfolio.** A single bad earnings report or regulatory ruling can hurt your whole return.

## A practical way to do this

1. **Keep most of your money in an index fund.** Put roughly 70 to 80% in an S&P 500 fund and use the other 20 to 30% for picks like these. That limits the damage if the picks lag.
2. **Split the picks equally**, at about 10% of that portion each, so no single stock dominates.
3. **Only use money you won't need for 3 to 5 years.** One year is short enough for a 20 to 30% drop.
4. **Write down why you bought each stock.** Sell if that reason stops being true, not just because the price moved.
5. **Consider taxes.** Short-term gains are often taxed at higher rates, and non-US investors may pay withholding tax on US dividends.

If you tell me your risk tolerance, time horizon and existing holdings, I can adjust the list, for example to make it more defensive or less dependent on AI.
